preamble: Raising and centralization of unstressed /e/ to the close central vowel [ɨ]. In European Portuguese, unstressed /a e o/ are raised to [ɐ ɨ u], and only [ɐ ɨ u] occur in final syllables. Stressed /e/ in peso /ˈpe.zu/ 'weight' therefore alternates with [ɨ] in pesar /pɨˈzaɾ/ 'to weigh', and dedo /ˈde.du/ 'finger' with dedal /dɨˈdal/ 'thimble'. Brazilian Portuguese keeps unstressed [e] (pesar /peˈza(ʁ)/, dedal /deˈdaw/). Descriptions write this vowel with different symbols: Wikipedia and Wiktionary write [ɨ] and Wikipedia's vowel chart places it at [ɯ̽], while Cruz-Ferreira (1995) writes /ɯ/, describing it as a fronted and lowered high back unrounded vowel that is often represented as /ə/. The atlas writes ɨ for all European Portuguese entries.

examples.from: pesar 'to weigh', unstressed e (cf. stressed peso /ˈpe.zu/ 'weight')
mesinha 'little table', unstressed e (cf. stressed mesa /ˈme.zɐ/ 'table')

sources: Cruz-Ferreira, M. (1995). European Portuguese. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 25(2), 90–94. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100300005223
